current_hypothesis: A genuinely different smooth candidate is to replace the singular toric polar chart by a smooth nonlinear slit-disk chart based on exterior log-polar coordinates, flatten each planar unit disk to a rectangle by an exact area-preserving map, and then reuse the standard l^2 square-slot packing in those smooth canonical coordinates.
stop_reason: Attempt 005 ruled out the naive smooth slit-chart square-slot family: although the planar chart is smooth and numerically correct, its best sampled ratios were only about 0.0769 for k=10 and 0.1230 for k=16, so generic area-coordinate rectangles destroy the toric packing mechanism.

last_summary.worked: Validated src/smooth_slit_chart_packing.py, a new smooth nonlinear slit-chart packing family. After the earlier fixes to the chart tables and angle branch handling, the planar chart had area_total approximately pi and roundtrip error below about 2e-11 in the relevant near-a=1 regime. Reproducible sweeps gave best sampled upper-bound ratios 0.07689370674740484 for k=10 and 0.12302993079584774 for k=16, both at a=1.01. Saved the main sweeps and diagnostic scans under results/research_loop/.
last_summary.did_not_work: The family failed decisively as a packing mechanism. Even in the perfect-square case k=16, where the toric square-slot family is exact, the smooth slit-chart family only achieved sampled ratio about 0.1230. For k=10 it only reached about 0.0769, which is about 12.3% of the toric square baseline 0.625 and about 11.1% of the better attempt_003 axis-block witness 0.6925. Because these ratios come from sampled boundary radii, they are optimistic upper bounds on the true ratio, so the actual performance can only be worse.
last_summary.next_step: Do not revisit generic slit-chart rectangle packings. The next construction should either smooth the toric/action variables while preserving a simplex-type relation analogous to x1+x2<=1, or switch to a fundamentally different non-affine folding family.
